why: n·k = 1,001 × 40 = 40,040 > 40,000, so stkOmegaBoot runs 200 resamples while the note says 400 (F13). Generated: mulberry32 (stkRng's mixer) seeded 1103, Box-Muller normals, 1,001 people with a factor score f, item j (j = 0..39) = round(3 + (0.2 + 0.4·((7j mod 10)/10))·f + 1.0·e) clamped to 1-5 (the draws in row order: f, then e for each item). The seed is one whose interval prints differently at 200 resamples ([.82, .84]) and at 400 ([.82, .85]), so the fixture tells the two apart. 40 items rather than the brief's 7,000 × 6: stkCorrMat's SD recomputes smean inside its reduce (n² per column), so a resample costs k·n²; 7,000 × 6 takes about 2 minutes per run in Node, 1,001 × 40 about 15 s. First in the file, so that the capture runs it before the small alpha cases (after them V8 runs stkCorrMat and stkOmega several times slower on this sample: the capture took 2:48 with the case last, 39 s with it first); the port runs it in its own test file, stats-slow.test.ts, and the two generic loops skip it
v1's alpha demo: q6 reversed on 1-5, the '(reversed)' label, 15 people (the n < 30 note)
the demo without rev: q6 unreversed lowers alpha
rev names an item that is not ticked: the 'Not found' toast
rev without rrange: the 'give the lowest and highest answer' toast
rrange 5-1: the 'highest must be larger' toast
rev matched case-insensitively and rrange written '1 to 5' with spaces: the same result as the demo
rrange written with an en dash, 1–5: the pattern's second separator, the same result as the demo
three identical items: alpha is exactly 1, so the interval is v1's [1,1] without stkFQuant
two items ticked: the 'at least 3 items' toast
q3 is 3 for everyone: stkCorrMat null, the 'same answer from everyone' toast
i5 is worded the other way: the 'correlates negatively' note
i5 barely loads: the 'correlates only weakly' note
near-copies of one item: alpha above .95 (and loadings near the ceiling)
two rows with an empty answer: '2 row(s) with a missing answer were left out.'
i3 is minus the sum of the other two: a negative alpha, every item negative with the rest, and i3's loading above 1, shown clamped to 1.00 with the ceiling note

four columns of an order-8 Hadamard design (1 as 4, -1 as 2): every inter-item correlation is exactly 0, so stkOmega's largest eigenvalue is exactly 0 and it returns null: omega and its interval are '–' and the 'could not be computed' note
